podcast.body: This single from Blind Melon's 1992 debut album, along with its famous "Bee Girl" video, was instrumental in the album's commercial success. "thanks largely to the single No Rain and the famous Bee Girl video."

podcast.body: This song is identified as the track that could lead to Blind Melon being labeled a one-hit wonder, a categorization that fans strongly dispute. The band's admirers emphasize the quality and quantity of their other recordings. "You can call Blind Melon, a one hit wonder for no rain."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Great Alt-Rock One-Hit Wonders of the 90s: Part 1

podcast.body: This song, from Blind Melon's self-titled debut album, became massively popular due to its accompanying music video. Shannon Hoon wrote the song for his girlfriend, who was dealing with depression and would often complain that sunny weather removed her excuse to stay indoors. While the song might sound happy, its underlying message is melancholic. "Blimeyellon and No Rain, a song he wrote for his girlfriend, was having a hard time with depression."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Death as a Career Move ｜ From the Archives

podcast.body: During a Halloween concert in Vancouver at the Pacific Colosseum on October 31, 1993, while opening-actpourlenty crabbits, frontman Shannon Hoon performed the final three songs, including "No Rain," completely naked. This celebration, fueled by the full moon and party atmosphere, escalated into simulating sex with a bee-costumed roadie and urinating on stage and into the front row audience. "The bee was there because the final song of the set was No Rain, and a bee, of course, figured prominently in the music video."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
